Key responsibilities and accomplishments included delivering Fusion’s next generation platform, managing a multi-million dollar departmental budget, maintaining near 90% employee retention, facilitating SOC2 compliance process, leading the department through an agile transformation, instilling best practices in software engineering, product management and quality assurance and serving as a culture warrior and process leader in the company.
As the Director of Technical Success, I built a highly-available, SaaS focused, services, customer support, operations and technical success team from the ground up - in the eDiscovery space.

Planned and managed development of a web-based application to help scale the company (a third-party logistics broker) at a rapid rate. Hired, trained, and managed engineers and interns through the development life cycle in a strict Agile environment. Reported directly to the CTO.

Served as a key member of the Agile software development team to solve business problems and streamline operations for this electronic stock-trading company. Recruited, hired, and mentored new team members while working side-by-side with peers to complete complex engineering projects.

Hired as Tools Developer and earned a series of promotions to Software Engineer, Senior Software Engineer, and Team Lead during five-year tenure. Managed several teams and led multiple engineering projects to support business operations.
Recognized as the only intern offered a staff QA Analyst position after completing a six-month internship in the technology department. Provided expertise, analysis, and support for QA projects.

Each year, 34 graduate students from across campus form interdisciplinary teams and collaborate to co-create actionable, high-impact solutions for the organizational partners they serve. headline: Senior Vice President at Citi                        Data and Business Process Re-engineering Sr. Manager
about:
I started my career at the Northern Trust mutual funds processing group.  I worked on various initiatives that helped automate the processing, reconciliation and trade communication of the third-party mutual funds through NSCC and transfer agencies.  

Upon successfully automating the spreadsheet driven mutual funds, my career focus shifted to alternative investments.  Although a manual asset class, I worked with a group of very talented partners on process redesign and workflow development that resulted in efficient and streamlined processing of transactions and valuation of alternative investments.  

Over the next few years my oversight not only included management of projects, but also business analysts and project managers who worked on projects related to alternative investments, cash and securities lending.  My efforts in this area enhanced efficiency and productivity with strong focus on the delivery of regulatory requirements.

As I continued to grow professionally, I ventured out to product management within the alternative investments group.  I managed the performance analytics product and launched the investment manager invoice processing product from ideation to implementation.  Most recently, my work includes the document ingestion and automation of the alternative investments using artificial intelligence.

In 2019, I moved to Citibank where I started in marketing, leading the Balance Transfer strategy.  My work consisted of refining strategies, presenting to leadership and upon approval, executing the marketing strategy.  Additionally, I led the balance transfer system related project work with technology.  

After two years in marketing, I moved to Business Simplification and Process Reengineering group and was promoted to SVP.  I led a variety of process improvement projects, consisting of centralization, process redesign and regulatory implications.

topSkills: Leadership • International Business • Private Wealth Management • Strategic Communications • Marketing
about:
Carla is a Senior Business Manager at Citi's Private Bank in Beverly Hills, CA. With over 20 years of global experience across the US, China, South Korea, and her native Brazil, she brings valuable cultural insights and management expertise to her role.

Carla joined Citi through its GEMA Program (a Leadership Development Program) and since then has held various positions within the organization, including Credit Cards Marketing, Sales and Trading, Export and Import Business, Corporate Banking, Finance, Operations, Recovery Planning, Blockchain Investing and International Franchise Management. 

Carla has been recognized by HISPA for her professional achievements and contributions to Diversity, Equity & Inclusion. During her 13-year journey at Citi, Carla has led multiple Diversity Equity & Inclusion efforts and committees, including as Chair of Citi's Latino & Hispanic Heritage Network and of the Families Matter Network - NY Chapter, which she helped found. She also collaborated with Citi’s Disability, Pride and Black Heritage Networks.
 
As a mother to Nina (5) and Lucas (8), Carla values family and mental well-being. This inspired her to found A Day to Remember Journals, a publishing hub and community for journal lovers, where she shares her passion for journaling and self-publishing as ways to develop self-care and to reach others.

projects.title: Numerical modeling of primary atomization of liquid fuel in aircraft engines
Analysis of Turbulent Combustion
projects.description: This project was for the Simulation Sciences Seminar course module. The objective of this project is to get better understanding of auto-ignition phenomenon in a non-premixed combustion. To this end, a temporal jet setup was taken into consideration in a channel flow configuration with n-heptane as fuel. DNS data for this setup was used for studying auto-ignition. The outcomes of this project include: most reactive mixture fraction for this setup at which the ignition first takes place was found out, temperature and heat release rate were identified as variables of auto-ignition, mixture fraction, scalar dissipation rate and reaction progress variable were identified as parameters using which auto-ignition could described.

projects.title: Unstructured FEM Solver for 2D Heat Diffusion
projects.description: This project was a part of Simulation Sciences Laboratory course module. A finite element based two-dimensional transient heat diffusion solver with triangular elements was developed in C++. A serial code was developed and optimized at the first stage. The results of the serial code was validated using analytical solutions. Then the serial code was parallelized using OpenMP and used to solve a transient heat transfer engineering problem.

projects.title: Eigenvalue Computation
projects.description:
This was implemented for a project as a part of Fast Iterative Solvers course module. Krylov method was implemented in finding the maximum and minimum eignevalues of a symmetric positive definite matrix. The maximum and minimum eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the matrix were computed using:
1. Power iteration and inverse iteration respectively
2. Lanczos method
The results from power iteration, inverse iteration and Lanczos method were compared for finding the better method with faster runtime in computing maximum and minimum eigenvalues of a matrix.

projects.title: MPI Parallelized FEM code for Structured Mesh
projects.description: This project was a part of Parallel Computing in Simulation Sciences course module. Serial FEM code for structured mesh implemented earlier was extended to parallel version using round robin algorithm with MPI parallel framework. The goal of the project was to understand the point to point communication among the processors in projecting the solution from coarse to a fine mesh.

projects.title: Multigrid Solver
projects.description: A multigrid solver was developed for a project as a part of Fast Iterative Solvers course module. In this project, a multigrid algoriithm was implemented for solving Poisson equation using a Finite Difference Cartesian grid.

projects.title: OpenMP Parallelized FEM code for Structured Mesh
projects.description: This project was a part of Parallel Computing in Simulation Sciences course module. Serial FEM code for structured mesh implemented earlier was now parallelized using OpenMP framework. The goal of this project was to compare the results from the parallel code to that of serial code, compare the scaling of the code with number of threads and to optimize the code

projects.title: Serial FEM Code for structured mesh
projects.description: This project was a part of Parallel Computing in Simulation Sciences course module. A structured FEM code was implemented in projecting the solution from a coarse to a fine tetrahedral mesh. The goal of the project is to implement a serial version of the code and optimize it.

projects.title: Sparse Linear Equation System Iterative Solver
projects.description:
A sparse linear equation system iterative solver was developed for a project as a part of Fast Iterative Solvers course module in M.Sc. Simulation Sciences study. The iterative solver was based on Krylov methods:
1. Generalized Minimum RESidual (GMRES) (full and restarted modes) with Jacobi and Gauss Seidel pre-conditioning for non-symmetric indefinite matrices
2. Conjugate Gradient (CG) for symmetric positive definite matrices

projects.title: Endoscopic Imaging of Early Flame Development
projects.description: This project was carried out on the selection DAAD Working Internships in Science and Engineering (WISE) Scholarship 2013 . The images of the combustion flames in a BMW Spark Ignition Engine were obtained using the Endoscope attached to the engine. The analysis of the flame was done for the OH radical in the flame. The two different images of the same flame was obtained by capturing the images by two cameras with a delay period and a 50/50 beam split was used to send light rays of the flame to both the cameras.The post processing of the early flame images were done using MATLAB and found the flame velocity.

projects.title: Production and Utilisation of Biodiesel in a Diesel Engine

projects.title: Steady Advection-Diffusion experiments
projects.description: This project was a part of Finite Elements in Fluids course module. In this project, a steady advection-diffusion equation was solved using XNS solver (developed at CATS, RWTH Aachen University). The goal of the project was to understand the various stabilization techniques such as Full Upwinding, Streamline Upwinding (SU) and Streamline Upwind Petrov Galerkin (SUPG). The results from the solver were compared to those in "Finite Element Methods for Flow Problems by John Donea and Antonio Huerta".

projects.title: Stokes and Navier-Stokes Experiments
projects.description: This project was a part of Finite Elements in Fluids course module. In this project, Stokes and Navier-Stokes equations were solved using XNS solver (developed at CATS, RWTH Aachen University). The problem setup was a lid-driven cavity. Two cases - with low and with high Reynolds number were considered for the same setup. In this project, incompressible Navier-Stokes equations were solved. The goal of the project was to understand how the solution varies with different stabilization techniques such as Streamline Upwind Petrov Galerkin (SUPG), Pressure Stabilized Petrov Galerkin (PSPG) for each case of the problem. The results from the solver were compared to those in "Finite Element Methods for Flow Problems by John Donea and Antonio Huerta".

projects.title: Unsteady Advection-Diffusion Experiments
projects.description: This project was a part of Finite Elements in Fluids course module. In this project, an unsteady advection-diffusion equation was solved using XNS solver (developed at CATS, RWTH Aachen University). Two initial conditions were undertaken in this study. The goal of the project was to understand how time and spatial stabilization techniques alter the solutions for each of the two initial conditions. The spatial stabilization techniques that were implemented include Streamline Upwind Petrov Galerkin (SUPG), Galerkin Least Squares (GLS) with Crank Nicolson time discretization scheme for temporal discretization. The results from the solver were compared to those in "Finite Element Methods for Flow Problems by John Donea and Antonio Huerta".

publications.title: A hybrid moment of fluid–level set framework for simulating primary atomization
publications.publishedAt: Journal of Computational Physics · Dec 9, 2021
publications.description: This paper presents a hybrid moment of fluid–level set (HyMOFLS) method of liquid/gas interface reconstruction for the application to simulate primary atomization of liquid fuel. This method combines the moment of fluid (MOF) method and the level set framework in the coupled level set volume of fluid (CLSVOF) method. In this hybrid method, the MOF and CLSVOF methods are used to reconstruct the interface in the under-resolved and the resolved regions of the flow, respectively. An interface surface resolution metric called interface resolution quality (IRQ) is introduced to identify and classify these two flow regions in the computational domain. Such a strategy classifies/tags each computational cell with MOF or CLSVOF method based on a threshold value for the IRQ. The MOF method uses liquid volume fraction as well as centroids of liquid and gas phases for the interface reconstruction. The CLSVOF method uses the level set for describing the interface and liquid volume fraction for conserving the mass. The phase centroids in the HyMOFLS method are computed and transported on-the-fly during the cell tagging process. The transport of the liquid volume fraction, level set, and the phase centroids are performed using a directionally split algorithm. This algorithm is coupled with the Navier-Stokes equations solver that uses ghost fluid method as well as consistent mass and momentum flux computation for the momentum equation. The hybrid framework is shown to be well capturing the liquid/gas interface belonging to thin and under-resolved structures that are often encountered in simulations of turbulent atomization of liquids. The proposed HyMOFLS method is found to achieve a good balance between the accuracy and the computational cost of reconstructing the liquid/gas interface for complex and turbulent atomization configurations.

publications.title: Detailed numerical simulations of primary atomization of airblasted liquid sheet
publications.publishedAt: International Journal of Multiphase Flow · Oct 14, 2021
publications.description: This paper investigates the characteristics of primary and secondary atomization of liquid fuel injected in an airblasted fashion, a common injection technique used in aircraft engines along with crossflow injection.

publications.title: DNS and LES of primary atomization of turbulent liquid jet injection into a gaseous crossflow environment
publications.publishedAt: Proceedings of the Combustion Institute · Sep 18, 2020
publications.description: In this paper, we study the primary atomization characteristics of liquid jet injected into a gaseous crossflow through direct numerical simulations (DNS) and large eddy simulations (LES). The DNS use a coupled level set volume of fluid (CLSVOF) sharp interface capturing method resolving all relevant scales to predict the drop size distribution (DSD) for drops larger than the grid spacing. The LES use a volume of fluid (VOF) diffused interface method modelling the sub grid droplets. The purpose of this paper is to provide a comparison of the results of drop data between DNS and LES. The simulations are performed for a liquid jet injection with liquid-gas momentum flux ratio of 6.6, liquid jet Reynolds number of 14,000 injected into a crossflowing air with Reynolds number 570,000 and Weber number of 330 at a liquid-to-gas density ratio of 10. Two distinct and simultaneous atomization/breakup mechanisms have been observed in the simulations: column/bag breakup and ligament/surface breakup. It was found that the DSDs obtained from the DNS and LES each follow a log-normal distribution based on their respective droplet diameter data. An overlap region exists between the individual DSDs from the DNS and LES when combined. The width of this overlap region decreases along the downstream direction. A log-normal distribution is found to be a good fit to the combined DSD incorporating both resolved and sub-grid droplets. This information is relevant for the secondary atomization simulations and modeling.

publications.title: A 3D Moment of Fluid method for simulating complex turbulent multiphase  ows
publications.publishedAt: Computers & Fluids · Nov 14, 2019
publications.description: This paper presents the moment of fluid method as a liquid/gas interface reconstruction method coupled with a mass momentum conservative approach within the context of numerical simulations of incompressible two-phase flows. This method tracks both liquid volume fraction and phase centroid for reconstructing the interface. The interface reconstruction is performed in a volume (and mass) conservative manner and accuracy of orientation of interface is ensured by minimizing the centroid distance between original and reconstructed interface. With two-phase flows, moment of fluid method is able to reconstruct interface without needing phase volume data from neighboring cells. The performance of this method is analyzed through various transport and deformation tests, and through simple two-phase flows tests that encounter changes in the interface topologies. Exhaustive mesh convergence study for the reconstruction error has been performed through various transport and deformation tests involving simple two-phase flows. It is then applied to simulate atomization of turbulent liquid diesel jet injected into a quiescent environment. The volume conservation error for the moment of fluid method remains small for this complex turbulent case.

publications.title: Coupled Level set moment of fluid method for simulating multiphase flows
publications.publishedAt: publication description In Proceedings of the ILASS Europe, 29th Annual Conference on Liquid Atomization and Spray Systems · Sep 4, 2019
publications.description: A coupled level set moment of fluid (CLSMOF) method for numerical simulation of multiphase flows is presented in this paper. This numerical method of liquid/gas interface capture is a hybrid of classical moment of fluid (MOF) method and coupled level set volume of fluid (CLSVOF) method. In this CLSMOF method, MOF interface reconstruction is used only for the under-resolved liquid structures while the level set function is used for the in- terface reconstruction for the resolved structures. This method combines the advantages of accurate capture of under-resolved liquid strucutres from MOF method and sharp interface representation by the level set function. The results presented in this paper demonstrates the ability and accuracy of the CLSMOF method to be as high as that of the MOF method while incurring relatively less computational expense. Finally, the application of CLSMOF method to simulation of turbulent diesel jet yeilded a very satisfactory volume conservation.

publications.title: A comparative study of DNS of airblast atomization using CLSMOF and CLSVOF methods
publications.publishedAt: In Proceedings of the ILASS Europe, 29th Annual Conference on Liquid Atomization and Spray Systems · Sep 4, 2019
publications.description: The results from direct numerical simulations (DNS) of planar pre-filming airblast atomization are presented in this paper. The configuration of the airblast atomization is inspired from a published experimental configuration of Gepperth et al (ICLASS 2012). The simulations have been performed using our in-house Navier-Stokes solver ARCHER. Two DNS have been performed each respectively using coupled level moment of fluid (CLSMOF) and coupled level set volume of fluid (CLSVOF) methods for liquid/gas interface reconstruction. The operating point investigated in the simula- tions correspond to aircraft altitude relight conditions. The DNS data are post-processed consistent to that of the experimental data to extract droplet and ligament statistics. The droplet diameter distribution from the simulations is found to be having satisfactory agreement with the experimental data. Two breakup mechanisms of atomization are observed: sheet breakup producing small droplets and ligament breakup producing medium and bulgy droplets. The CLSMOF method is observed to produce more medium and bulgy droplets owing to dominant ligament breakup while CLSVOF method produced more number of small droplets owing to predominant sheet breakup mechanism. A good agreement was found between simulations and experiments for Sauter Mean Diameter (SMD) of the droplets. The droplet diameter distribution from the simulations are found to under-predict the peak of the distribution but displays similar profile as that of the experiments. The droplet velocity distribution from the simulations is found to agree well with that of the experiments. The liquid ligaments formed at the trailing edge of the pre-filmer plate are characterized by their lengths. The breakup length of the ligaments, defined as arithmetic mean of the ligament lengths, computed from the simulations agree satisfactorily with the value computed from the experimental data.

publications.title: Validation and Analysis of primary atomization of turbulent liquid jet in crossflow simulations
publications.publishedAt: ILASS Americas, 30th Annual Conference on Liquid Atomization and Spray Systems. Tempe, Arizona, USA · May 15, 2019
publications.description: This paper presents the results from direct numerical simulations of the primary atomization of a turbulent liquid jet injected into liquid crossflow. The simulations are performed for an experimentally analyzed configuration of Brown and McDonell (2006, “Near Field Behavior of a Liquid Jet in a Crossflow”, ILASS Americas, 19th Annual Conference on Liquid Atomization and Spray Systems). The turbulent liquid jet (q = 6.6, Re = 14 000, We = 2178) is injected into a subsonic gaseous crossflow (Re = 570 000, We = 330). The liquid/gas interface is captured using a coupled level set volume of fluid (CLSVOF) method. The jet penetration obtained from the simulations show good agreement with the experimental correlations and also to the findings from the literature. Two breakup mechanisms are observed: column breakup mode in which waves on the windward side of the jet propagate, roll up and form bag-like structures until they breakup; and ligament breakup mode caused by the corrugations of the liquid core surface forming thin ligaments on the liquid jet sides that subsequently breakup into droplets. Analysis of the crossflow velocity component of the liquid packets from the simulation shows that a number of liquid packets exist in the domain whose velocities are same as that of the gaseous crossflow.

publications.title: Validation and Analysis of 3D DNS of planar pre-filming airblast atomization simulations
publications.publishedAt: ILASS Americas, 30th Annual Conference on Liquid Atomization and Spray Systems. Tempe, Arizona, USA · May 15, 2019
publications.description: In this paper, results from direct numerical simulations (DNS) of published experimental configuration of planar pre-filming airblast atomization are presented. The simulations have been performed using our in- house multiphase Navier-Stokes equations solver ARCHER. The coupled level set volume of fluid (CLSVOF) method has been used for capturing the liquid/gas interface within the context of multiphase flows. This numerical method has been proved to well capture the interface from many of our previous works. A kerosene based fuel at an operating point corresponding to aircraft altitude relight conditions have been used in DNS. The results are analyzed in two parts: analysis of liquid droplets and analysis of liquid ligaments at the trailing edge of the pre-filmer plate. The analyses of the liquid droplets diameter and velocity distributions revealed that the results from the simulations are agreeing with the experimental data very satisfactorily. Moreover, the observation from these distributions is that the sheet breakup mechanism is dominant over the ligament breakup mechanism of atomization. Ligament analysis has been carried out by reducing the 3D DNS data to 1D liquid/gas interface contour. The frequency distribution of the liquid ligaments shows the under-prediction on their lengths in comparison to experiments. Overall, a satisfactory agreement has been achieved between the DNS and experiments.

publications.title: An investigation of characteristics of airblast atomization using 3D DNS for altitude relight conditions
publications.publishedAt: 11th U.S. National Combustion Meeting, Pasadena, California, USA · Mar 27, 2019
publications.description: This paper presents results from direct numerical simulations (DNS) of planar pre- filming airblast atomization. The liquid/gas interface has been captured using coupled level set moment of fluid method. This method is a hybrid between moment of fluid and coupled level set volume of fluid methods. The numerical method has been applied to airblast atomization analyzed experimentally by Gepperth et al. (2012, “Ligament and Droplet Characteristics in Prefilming Air- blast Atomization”, ICLASS 2012). The operating point investigated in this work correspond to aircraft altitude relight condition. The post-processing of the DNS data is performed consistently with that for the experimental data. The main mode of breakup observed is torn sheet breakup. A good agreement was found between simulations and experiments for Sauter Mean Diameter and droplet streamwise velocity distribution while satisfactory agreement has been found for the droplet diameter distribution and ligament breakup length.

publications.title: Numerical study of interface reconstruction method in under-resolved regions of the flow for liquid jet primary breakup
publications.publishedAt: 14th International Conference on Liquid Atomization and Spray Systems, Chicago, Illinois, USA · Jul 23, 2018
publications.description: Liquid/gas interface reconstruction continues to be a challenge in the numerical study of liquid fuel atomization. This paper focuses on one such reconstruction method called moment of fluid (MOF) method intended specifically for interface reconstruction in under-resolved flow regions. MOF method gives two-fold advantage over volume of fluid (VOF), level set (LS), and coupled level set volume of fluid (CLSVOF), such as: first, MOF preserves the shape and orientation of interfaces that are commonly encountered in under-resolved regions of the flow, and second, it exhibits second-order accuracy in spatial resolution for multiple interface topologies. For various test cases considered in this paper, MOF has consistently proved to be more accurate than and at least as accurate as CLSVOF method.

publications.title: Interface reconstruction method for multiphase flows in under-resolved regions
publications.publishedAt: 10th International Conference on Computational Fluid Dynamics (ICCFD10), Barcelona, Spain · Jul 10, 2018
publications.description: This paper presents an interface reconstruction method called moment of fluid (MOF) method for two-phase flows using statistical moments of liquid volume fraction. In each flow solver grid cell, the liquid volume fraction and liquid center of mass are used for computing the interface unit normal. The transport of the liquid volume fraction and center of mass is performed by a directionally split advection scheme. This method is validated, results are compared with those from coupled level set volume of fluid (CLSVOF) method for 2D and 3D test cases, and is found to be at least second--order accurate in spatial resolution. Furthermore, MOF method is shown to outperform CLSVOF method in terms of interface reconstruction for thin and under--resolved liquid ligaments and filaments thereby conserving mass in the domain.

publications.title: Numerical Study of Auto-Ignition in a Liquid n-heptane Jet
publications.publishedAt: 10th U.S. National Combustion Meeting, College Park, Maryland, USA · Apr 26, 2017
publications.description: Three-dimensional Direct Numerical Simulations (DNS) are performed for studying auto-ignition of liquid n-heptane spray at a pressure of 3.5 bar. A temporal mixing layer configuration is used to study to auto-ignition behavior in the presence of high temperature oxidizer. The liquid phase is represented using poly-dispersed spherical droplets tracked numerically in the Lagrangian frame of reference. A chemical mechanism consisting of 42 species and 304 elementary reactions is considered to represent finite-rate chemical kinetics of oxidation of n-heptane. From the numerical simulations, the most reactive (MR) value of mixture fraction was identified and was found to lie on the fuel lean side. The analysis of relationship between auto-ignited kernels and scalar dissipation rate showed that initial ignition kernels are formed in regions of lower scalar dissipation rate, in other words, regions of longer mixing time scales. To distinguish between the ignition and deflagration flame front, a criterion based on time scales of ignition and deflagration fronts was used. Using that criterion, it was observed that premixed flame initiates as an ignition front and transforms to a deflagration front thus consuming large regions of the domain and producing more heat release.

publications.title: Spray combustion and dissipation elements: a novel analysis approach
publications.publishedAt: European Combustion Meeting (ECM2017), Dubrovnik, Croatia · Apr 21, 2017
publications.description: In this work, Dissipation Element Analysis (DEA) is applied to Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) data of spray combustion. Both mixture fraction and temperature fields are analyzed at different times during the auto-ignition process. Marginal and joint statistics of DE parameters are shown and compared to those of DNS of isotropic homogeneous turbulence. A new length scale appearing only prior to ignition is identified. Possible modeling approaches resulting from the obtained statistics are sketched out.

projects.title: Spatial-Temporal Modeling of Weather Data
projects.description: This paper presents spatial-temporal modeling, an area that I researched during my MS and that introduced me to the kriging methods in statistics. In the first part, I give an overview of spatial processes, stationarity and isotropy, and how to describe the dependence structure through a covariance function or a variogram. These concepts are then extended to space-time processes, including an outline of some classes of covariance functions. Next, simple, ordinary and universal kriging are discussed, and in the last section I present a real-world application of kriging when applied to the 2020 temperature data in Illinois.

projects.title: US Flight Delays Prediction

projects.title: Exploration of Tree-based Methods for Regression and Classification

Packages used: tidyverse, tree, rpart, randomForest, gbm, caret, arm, class.

about:
With more than 15 years as an Executive Transformational Leader, I have a background spanning strategic initiatives and innovative product launches. I am well versed in cross-functional team leadership, analytical problem-solving, P&L management, and stakeholder engagement. It is my passion to leverage a solid financial and business acumen to drive growth while executing large-scale and complex projects for Fortune 500 companies.
  
Key Achievements Include: 

✅  Spearheaded digital business strategy for 37 leading US retailers, managing a cross-functional team of 5, a $1.5M budget, and generating $40M in revenue through product initiatives, co-brand, and private label offerings for clients including Macy's, Home Depot, and Citi

✅  Pioneered first Agile transformation in an acquisition channel, leading to adoption of SAFe methodology across 75+ projects

✅  Championed a Lean management system transition across 5 business lines with a $500K budget, leading a team of 10 managers and supporting 15 senior leaders, effectively streamlining operations and enhancing international presence

✅  Spearheaded 50+ major corporate initiatives across card, bank, and payment businesses, generating $21M in new sales

✅  Leveraged entrepreneurial mindset to create product vision and launch Discover’s new Secured Card, managing end-to-end projects within a $2M budget, creating new market segments, and expanding reach to individuals with low credit scores. 

Contact me through this profile if you wish to connect.

experience.position: Senior Vice President of Emerging Products & Change Management (Chicago, IL)
experience.description:
